outcomes: Each Gradle project, Android included, and each Maven module that packages code is a Putnami project, with an edge to each component it depends on in the same build
putnami lint, test and build run the steps of the component's build, Gradle wrapper or Maven, in its directory, and a second run over an unchanged tree is a cache hit
The test task reads the JUnit reports and the JaCoCo report the build writes into the test and coverage summary
A change under src/test reruns test, never lint
A component overrides any value of the Java profile in its putnami.json, and the override reaches the cache key
nonGoals: Installing or switching a JDK, Gradle or Maven: the toolchain check compares and never installs
Comparing the Gradle wrapper's version with the machine: the wrapper downloads the version it names, and its properties file reaches the key
A Gradle or Maven build whose root is not the Putnami workspace root, and Gradle composite builds
Android product flavors: a flavored app overrides the test step
Publishing an artifact to a repository

requirements.text: The probe answers, for each candidate directory the observe Gradle or Maven detector knows as a component: a project named by the Gradle path without its leading colon, ':' turned into '/', or by the Maven artifactId (no name for the Gradle root project, which keeps its directory's name), the directories of the components it depends on, the extension @putnami/java, the tag java, and metadata naming the build's reference of the component (the Gradle task path prefix, ':' for the root project and ':api:' for :api, or the Maven groupId:artifactId), its variant, the stack root '.' and the expected Java version. A directory that both builds claim is the Gradle build's. A directory with no component is no project.

A Maven module is variant maven. A Gradle project whose build file applies an Android plugin or holds an android block is variant android, or android-coverage when it enables unit test coverage; any other Gradle project is gradle, or gradle-jacoco when its build file applies the jacoco plugin. Each variant is a part of the profile applied before the project's override.

Each task first compares java -version with the version .java-version states, in the component then at the root: a major such as 21 matches every 21.x release. It then runs the variant's steps in the component's directory with no shell: for Gradle, the root's gradlew with the component's task path ({component}check -x {component}test for lint, {component}test for test, {component}assemble for build; testDebugUnitTest and assembleDebug for Android; jacocoTestReport and createDebugUnitTestCoverageReport after the tests for the coverage variants), for Maven, mvn --batch-mode --file {root}/pom.xml --projects {component} --also-make with verify -DskipTests for lint, verify for test and package -DskipTests for build.

The test task reads the JUnit reports, build/test-results/test (testDebugUnitTest for Android) or target/surefire-reports, and the JaCoCo XML report, build/reports/jacoco/test, build/reports/coverage/test/debug or target/site/jacoco, into the test and coverage summary. A component with no file under src/test expects no report. A Maven module without a JaCoCo report reads none; for the coverage variants a missing report fails the task with stacks.report_missing.

The java:lint selector answers the main sources, the build files and the lint configurations, never src/test or the lockfiles, so a change under src/test or to a lockfile reruns test and build and keeps lint's key.

options["@putnami/java"] in a component's own putnami.json overrides its variant's profile: an object merges, any other value replaces the variant's whole. The steps run and the files the java:<task> selectors answer follow the resolved profile, and putnami.json is an input of every task. An unknown member, a change to id, markers or variants, or a stack-root input the manifest does not declare fails the task with stacks.project_config_invalid.

The manifest passes the stack core's conformance kit: its markers are the profile's, it lists the java:lint, java:test and java:build selectors, and each command runs one task that depends on the same task upstream, reads its selector and every variant's stack-root files for that task, and declares its command-output reports directory.
